title: Vulnerable components runner: detect known CVEs in running web application libraries via response fingerprinting and dependency analysis
goal: WebGoat has a 'vulnerablecomponents' module (OWASP A06:2021 - Vulnerable and Outdated Components). AegisPT has CVE matching for discovered hosts/services but no web application component fingerprinting. Implement a vuln-components runner: (1) HTTP Response Fingerprinting: analyse HTTP response headers (X-Powered-By, Server, X-AspNet-Version), HTML comments, and JavaScript files to identify framework versions (jQuery 1.6.4, Spring 4.3.18, Apache Struts 2.3.x, etc.). (2) JavaScript library version detection: scan all linked JS files for version strings (jquery.min.js?v=1.6.4, bootstrap version comments). Match against CVE database. (3) npm/package.json exposure: check for accidentally exposed package.json, yarn.lock, package-lock.json files at common paths. Extract dependency list and match against CVE database. (4) Maven/Gradle exposure: check for exposed pom.xml (common on Java apps like WebGoat). (5) Match found versions against local CVE feed (using existing cve_sync infrastructure). (6) Tool: use RetireJS for JavaScript library scanning, OWASP Dependency Check for Java apps (passive — reads exposed files, no active exploitation). (7) Produces findings: 'Outdated Library: jQuery 1.6.4 (CVE-2019-11358 - prototype pollution)', 'Exposed package.json with vulnerable dependencies'. Active tier.
scope: Gap analysis 2026-05-03: WebGoat vulnerablecomponents module. OWASP A06:2021 is a top-10 category. AegisPT currently has no capability to detect vulnerable web application libraries. Burp Suite + Retire.js extension does this automatically. This is a high-value, relatively low-risk addition.
generation_reason: OWASP A06 (Vulnerable Components) missing from AegisPT — WebGoat has dedicated module and Burp Suite detects automatically via Retire.js.
